title: autonomous-telemetry-freshness-guard-and-safe-mitigation-defer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds autonomous telemetry-freshness scoring to incident contexts, ephemeral snapshot replay for debugging, and a deferred mitigation scheduler with safety gates. No breaking API changes. Backward compatible RBAC checks added.
description:
Motivation: On several recent page incidents we observed that responders were chasing stale telemetry (metric windows > 2min old) or taking mitigation steps without a fresh snapshot of traces/logs. This PR implements a lightweight 'Telemetry Freshness Guard' to surface a freshness score and annotate incidents when the observed telemetry is likely 'ghosting'. It also introduces an Ephemeral Snapshot Replayer for quick, sanitized context rehydration and a Deferred Mitigation Playback flow that lets on-call schedule safe mitigations with approvals and automatic rollbacks if health checks fail.

What this changes (high level): - Telemetry freshness heuristic and scoring added to the incident enrichment pipeline; score is exposed as incident.metadata.freshness_score and a short human-readable rationale. - Snapshot capture: minimal traces, recent spans, compact log tail, and request-level KV snapshot stored encrypted with KMS; snapshots are short-lived (TTL default 1h) and accessible via signed replay sessions. - Ephemeral Replay UI + CLI (ibctl snapshot replay <id>) that streams reconstructed context into the incident timeline for responders. - Deferred mitigations: runbook actions can be scheduled with safety gates (pre-checks, cooldowns, reviewer approvals). Actions are idempotent by design and stamped with action tokens for audit. - Operational controls: rate limits for snapshot creation, RBAC gating for mitigation scheduling, audit logs emitted to the existing audit pipeline.

Implementation notes: - New background worker (incident-freshness-processor) subscribes to incident enrichment queue and calculates freshness_score using metric ingestion timestamps and trace spans. Uses Redis to cache last-observed-window per service to avoid repeated work. - Snapshot storage introduced as incident_snapshots table (light index on incident_id) with encrypted payloads; short TTL enforced by a cleanup job. - Deferred mitigation scheduler persists action plans and runs a pre-flight check harness (synthetic health probes). If probes fail, the action is automatically cancelled and responders are notified. - Safety-first defaults: all deferred actions default to "require reviewer approval" for non-low risk labels; admins can relax policy via console. - Telemetry and metrics: added prometheus counters for snapshot_create, snapshot_replay_latency, freshness_score_histogram, deferred_action_attempts/success/failure.

Tests and verification: - Unit tests for freshness heuristics and RBAC checks. - Integration tests for snapshot capture/replay using sanitized synthetic traces. - E2E staged test that creates a synthetic alert, captures a snapshot, replays it into the incident timeline and schedules a deferred mitigation, verifying pre-checks and audit log entries. - Load test: snapshot creation path benchmarked at 2000 rps in staging with median latency increase of ~45ms under baseline load (within SLO).

Commits (summary): - Add freshness scoring engine and enrichment consumer - Implement incident_snapshots table and snapshot encoder/decoder - Add snapshot CLI + replay endpoint with signed sessions - Deferred mitigation scheduler + preflight harness - RBAC checks, audit hooks, and prometheus metrics - Docs and runbook updates - Fix flake in snapshot encoder tests

Files changed (high level): - cmd/ibctl/snapshot.go (CLI commands) - services/incident/enrichment/freshness_processor.go - services/incident/storage/snapshot_store.go - services/incident/handlers/replay_handler.go - services/mitigation/scheduler.go - db/migrations/20250729_create_incident_snapshots.up.sql - webapp/src/components/SnapshotReplay.tsx - infra/redis/worker-config.yaml - docs/runbooks/oncall-snapshot-replay.md

Review summary and rollout: - Initial CI run failed due to a flaky encoder test (flaky seed generation). Fixed by normalizing timestamps in encoder and re-running. - Security review by Lena: requested explicit KMS key rotation note and an extra audit field; implemented. - SRE review by Omar: requested rate limit default of 10/min per team and a circuit-breaker on replay; implemented. - Diego suggested making preflight probes configurable per runbook; addressed with a config flag and added a unit test. - After approval, rolled out in canary to staging for 48h, then to production with a feature flag. Flags default enabled for internal teams and opt-in for customers.

Merge outcome: PR was squashed and merged. Post-merge actions included adding a short notice to #oncall and running a migration during a low-traffic window.
review_thread:
Omar Patel: Nice approach. Two asks: add a circuit-breaker for replay (so a bad snapshot can't overload services) and tighten the default rate-limit.
Maya Chen: Added circuit-breaker using a semaphore with exponential backoff and set default to 10/min/team; updated tests and docs.

Lena Fischer: Security review: ensure snapshots are encrypted and include KMS rotation notes + audit field for snapshot_creator.
Maya Chen: Snapshots are encrypted via KMS; added snapshot_creator, created_at, and rotation guidance in docs.

Diego Marques: Can the deferred action preflight be overridable for runbook authors?
Maya Chen: Added runbook-level config and wrote unit tests to cover preflight toggles.
